questions.question: Which rocket launched Aditya-L1?

explanation.text: Aditya-L1 was launched aboard a PSLV rocket.

questions.question: What is Astrosat, launched by ISRO in 2015?

options.content: India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory

explanation.text: Astrosat observes celestial objects across X-ray, ultraviolet and visible light simultaneously.

questions.question: What does XPoSat, launched by ISRO on 1 January 2024, study?

options.content: The polarisation of X-rays from cosmic sources like black holes and neutron stars

explanation.text: XPoSat (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite) studies the polarisation of X-rays from extreme cosmic sources.

questions.question: XPoSat made India only the ___ country to launch a dedicated X-ray polarimetry mission, after the USA's IXPE.

explanation.text: XPoSat made India the second country, after the US, to fly a dedicated X-ray polarimetry mission.

questions.question: What is Gaganyaan, ISRO's most ambitious current programme?

explanation.text: Gaganyaan aims to send Indian astronauts to low Earth orbit aboard an indigenous spacecraft.

questions.question: What does the word 'Gaganyaan' roughly mean?

explanation.text: 'Gaganyaan' combines 'gagan' (sky) and 'yaan' (vehicle/craft).

questions.question: Which rocket, a human-rated version of the LVM3, is set to carry Gaganyaan's crew to orbit?

explanation.text: HLVM3 is the human-rated variant of the LVM3 (GSLV Mk III) developed for crewed flight.

questions.question: What is Vyommitra, expected to fly on early uncrewed Gaganyaan test flights?

options.content: A humanoid robot that simulates crew functions

explanation.text: Vyommitra is a humanoid robot built to test and validate systems before astronauts fly.

questions.question: Vyommitra's name combines Sanskrit words roughly meaning:

explanation.text: 'Vyom' means sky/space and 'mitra' means friend.

questions.question: How many Indian Air Force pilots were originally selected as astronaut-designates for Gaganyaan?

explanation.text: Four IAF test pilots - Prasanth Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap and Shubhanshu Shukla - were selected as Gaganyaan astronaut-designates.

questions.question: Which Gaganyaan astronaut-designate became the first Indian to visit the International Space Station, flying on a private mission in 2025?

explanation.text: Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the ISS aboard the commercial Axiom Mission 4 in 2025.

questions.question: Roughly how long is Gaganyaan's first crewed mission expected to keep astronauts in low Earth orbit?

explanation.text: Gaganyaan's first crewed flight is planned as a short mission of a few days in low Earth orbit.

questions.question: Who is the first Indian citizen to travel into space, doing so in 1984?

explanation.text: Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space in 1984.

questions.question: Rakesh Sharma flew to space aboard which spacecraft, as part of a joint Indo-Soviet mission?

explanation.text: Rakesh Sharma flew aboard Soyuz T-11 to the Soviet Salyut 7 space station.

questions.question: When asked by the Indian Prime Minister how India looked from space, what did Rakesh Sharma famously reply?

explanation.text: Sharma's famous reply, quoting the poem, means 'better than the whole world'.

questions.question: Which astronaut of Indian origin became the first Indian-born woman to fly to space, in 1997?

explanation.text: Kalpana Chawla flew her first Space Shuttle mission (STS-87) in 1997.

questions.question: Kalpana Chawla tragically lost her life in which spacecraft disaster in 2003?

explanation.text: Kalpana Chawla died when Space Shuttle Columbia broke apart during re-entry in February 2003.

questions.question: Which American astronaut of Indian origin is known for setting records for cumulative spacewalk time by a woman?

explanation.text: Sunita Williams, of Indian and Slovenian descent, has set multiple records for spacewalking.

questions.question: In 2025, which Indian Air Force officer became the first Indian to visit the International Space Station?

explanation.text: Shubhanshu Shukla became the first Indian to visit the ISS, flying on Axiom Mission 4.

questions.question: Shubhanshu Shukla travelled to the ISS aboard which kind of mission?

explanation.text: He flew as part of the privately organised Axiom Mission 4 to the ISS.

questions.question: Shubhanshu Shukla's 2025 spaceflight made him the ___ Indian citizen to go to space (after Rakesh Sharma).

explanation.text: He became only the second Indian citizen ever to travel to space, 41 years after Rakesh Sharma.

questions.question: On 15 February 2017, ISRO's PSLV-C37 mission set a world record. What was it?

options.content: Launching 104 satellites in a single mission

explanation.text: PSLV-C37 deployed a then world-record 104 satellites in one launch.

questions.question: India's Mars Orbiter Mission is often compared for its low cost to which Hollywood film's production budget?

explanation.text: MOM's total cost (about $74 million) was famously noted as being less than the reported budget of the film Gravity.

questions.question: What is NISAR, a satellite jointly developed by ISRO and NASA, launched in 2025?

explanation.text: NISAR uses dual-frequency synthetic aperture radar to monitor changes on Earth's surface.

questions.question: What does the 'SAR' in NISAR stand for?

explanation.text: SAR stands for Synthetic Aperture Radar, a remote-sensing radar imaging technique.

questions.question: What is India's proposed space station, planned for the late 2020s and 2030s, called?

explanation.text: ISRO plans to build the Bharatiya Antariksh Station as India's own orbital outpost.

questions.question: Around which year does ISRO aim to launch the first module of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station?

explanation.text: ISRO has targeted 2028 for the first module, with the full station envisioned by 2035.

questions.question: What is the name of ISRO's planned mission to Venus?

explanation.text: Shukrayaan (from 'Shukra', the Sanskrit name for Venus) is ISRO's planned Venus orbiter.

questions.question: What is the name of ISRO's planned follow-up Mars mission, also called the Mars Lander Mission?

explanation.text: Mangalyaan-2 (Mars Lander Mission) is ISRO's planned follow-up mission to Mars.

questions.question: What is Chandrayaan-4, a mission ISRO is currently developing?

explanation.text: Chandrayaan-4 is planned as India's first lunar sample-return mission.

questions.question: NAVIC is India's own satellite system, mainly used for:

options.content: Navigation and positioning, similar to GPS

explanation.text: NAVIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) provides accurate positioning services over India and the surrounding region.

questions.question: What does 'NAVIC' stand for?

options.content: National Aviation and Vehicle Information Centre

explanation.text: NAVIC stands for Navigation with Indian Constellation.

questions.question: Which ISRO programme is developing reusable rocket technology to reduce launch costs, similar in concept to reusable rockets flown elsewhere?

explanation.text: ISRO's RLV-TD (Reusable Launch Vehicle - Technology Demonstrator) programme is testing reusable rocket technology.

questions.question: Who is the Chairman of ISRO as of 2026?

explanation.text: Dr. S Somanath took over as ISRO Chairman in 2022 and has been leading the organisation through 2026.

questions.question: Which agency is ISRO's partner in the United States, with whom it jointly built the NISAR satellite?

explanation.text: NASA and ISRO jointly developed and launched the NISAR Earth-observation satellite.

questions.question: What made India's Chandrayaan-3 landing especially significant compared to earlier Moon landings by other countries?

options.content: It was the first-ever Moon landing
It was the first successful landing near the Moon's south pole
It carried the first animal to the Moon
It was the fastest Moon landing

explanation.text: Chandrayaan-3 was the first mission by any country to successfully soft-land near the lunar south pole.

questions.question: Which facility trains India's Gaganyaan astronaut-designates in Bengaluru?

options.content: The Human Space Flight Centre, ISRO

explanation.text: ISRO's Human Space Flight Centre in Bengaluru oversees astronaut training and mission preparation.

questions.question: What professional background do all four of Gaganyaan's original astronaut-designates share?

options.content: They are all Indian Air Force test pilots
They are all engineers with no flying experience

explanation.text: All four were experienced test pilots from the Indian Air Force.

questions.question: Which of these ISRO missions is focused on studying the Sun, rather than the Moon or Mars?

explanation.text: Aditya-L1 is dedicated to solar observation, unlike the other missions listed.

questions.question: Which of these is a genuinely planned or ongoing ISRO project as of 2026?

options.content: A crewed mission to Mars by 2026
A permanent Indian base on Venus

explanation.text: The Bharatiya Antariksh Station is an active, planned ISRO programme; the other options are not real ISRO plans.

questions.question: What is the main long-term goal of ISRO's human spaceflight efforts, starting with Gaganyaan?

options.content: To copy other countries' space programmes exactly
To develop India's independent capability to safely send humans to space and back
To replace all of ISRO's uncrewed satellites
To build a colony on the Moon immediately

explanation.text: Gaganyaan is meant to establish India's own indigenous human spaceflight capability.

questions.question: Before flying to the ISS in 2025, what had already made Shubhanshu Shukla notable within ISRO's human spaceflight programme?

options.content: He was one of the four IAF pilots selected as a Gaganyaan astronaut-designate

explanation.text: Shukla was already training as one of the four Gaganyaan astronaut-designates before his 2025 ISS flight.

questions.question: Besides Rakesh Sharma and Shubhanshu Shukla, which American astronaut of Indian origin commanded the International Space Station?

explanation.text: Sunita Williams served as commander of the International Space Station during Expedition 33.

questions.question: Sirisha Bandla, a woman of Indian origin, became known in 2021 for flying to space with which company?

explanation.text: Sirisha Bandla flew aboard Virgin Galactic's Unity 22 suborbital flight in July 2021.

questions.question: What does IN-SPACe, a body set up by the Indian government, mainly do?

options.content: Promotes and regulates private and non-governmental space activities in India

explanation.text: IN-SPACe encourages and regulates private-sector participation in India's space activities.

questions.question: Which private Indian company launched Vikram-S in November 2022, India's first privately developed rocket?

explanation.text: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S became India's first privately built rocket to reach space.

questions.question: ISRO is developing a new spaceport at Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu, mainly to:

options.content: Serve as a new launch site, especially for smaller satellite launch vehicles

explanation.text: The Kulasekarapattinam spaceport is being built as a new launch site to support smaller rockets like the SSLV.
